nurses' turnover intention is negatively correlated to job satisfaction, work, engagement and self efficacy and positively correlated to patient satisfaction.

nurses' self efficacy, agenic capacities, job satisfaction and work engagement have a significant influence on their turnover intention and that patient satisfaction is influenced by nurses' job satisfaction and work engagements.
nurses who are satisfied with their job, who are engaged in their work and who have a strong sense of self-efficacy are less likely to leave their jobs.

a new approach to nurses' turnover, which is based on the analysis of nurses' agentic capacities.
the development of nurses' self efficacy, agenic capacities and work engagement to reduce nurses' voluntary turnover.
the development of a model of nurses' turnover and patient satisfaction, and the identification of the main factors that influence these two variables.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

nurses' turnover intention is a complex phenomenon which is influenced by multiple variables and that the most important of these variables are job satisfaction, self efficacy and some agentic capacities.

the results suggest the importance of improving the self efficacy and agental capacities of nurses, and of enhancing job satisfaction and work engagement to reduce nurses' voluntary turnover intention and increase patients' satisfaction with nursing care.

the results of this research suggest that the development of self efficacy and self regulation skills, job satisfaction, work satisfaction and engagement are all important in reducing nurses' turnover intentions, and that these factors are positively correlated with patient satisfaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of nurses' agentic capacities and self efficacy can improve their job satisfaction and work engagement, which in turn can reduce turnover intention, and increase patient satisfaction.
self efficacy and self regulation skills are important to improve nurses' work engagement and job satifaction.
nurses with higher levels of self efficacy, job satisfaction and work engagement, and who are better at anticipation and self regulation, are less likely to leave their job.

nurses' job satisfaction is a crucial variable for both nurses and patients.
the nurse manager can play a key role in reducing turnover and increasing patient satisfaction.
